messages:
diane_billing: Heads up -- Wire for INV-4120 (USD 14,200) was returned by our bank with reason 'beneficiary information incomplete'. Customer claims they sent the exact MT103 but their bank didn't include beneficiary address. Need quick remediation - invoice due tomorrow. @marc_treasury @csm_john

marc_treasury: Paste the return notice if you have it. Some correspondent banks are strict about beneficiary address for USD wires (esp. for non-US beneficiaries).

diane_billing: Bank return text: ```RETURN: MT103 REF: 2026-5591; revReason=BEN_INFO_INCOMPLETE; details='Missing beneficiary address: line2 or city required'```

csm_john: Customer (Panea Inc) says their bank only included beneficiary name and account. Their treasury team is remote and slow. They asked if we can accept partial credit and reconcile later.

marc_treasury: Two practical paths: 1) Ask them to resend the wire with beneficiary address included (fastest if their bank can re-issue same day), 2) Accept a card/ACH fallback today and refund when original wire clears (needs consent), 3) Accept a SWIFT copy + payer email and process a manual top-up (more manual ops).

diane_billing: Invoice is due tomorrow and customer prefers to avoid extra bank fees. They can do a card payment now but their procurement policy disallows charging cards over $10k without CFO sign-off. This is $14.2k.

legal_sam: If we accept card fallback, we need documented written consent from the payer (email OK) to charge the card for the outstanding amount. For amounts > $10k, ensure the approver (CFO) is cc'd in that consent to avoid disputes later.

csm_john: Reached out to their AP and CFO. CFO said they can approve card charge via signed email but prefer to resend the wire. They asked if we can extend due date by 72 hours while they coordinate with their bank.

marc_treasury: We can grant a 72-hour extension and mark the invoice as 'pending re-wire / remittance expected'. Meanwhile, create a temporary payment hold flag so our collections workflow doesn't auto-escalate. If they push the wire, ask them to include full beneficiary address exactly as on our bank record: Redwood Inference, 255 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105.

diane_billing: Noted. Email to AP drafted: "We received a return from our bank indicating beneficiary address was missing. Please resend the USD wire ensuring the beneficiary address matches our records EXACTLY: Redwood Inference, 255 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105. If you need to pay immediately, reply with a signed email authorizing a card charge and cc your CFO; otherwise we can extend the due date 72 hours while you reissue the wire." Sending now. cc @marc_treasury

payments-bot: Logged return event for INV-4120. Flagging invoice as payment_issue:ben_info_incomplete. Created payment ticket PT-1961000123. Dunning paused for 72h. Please upload remittance or signed consent when available.

bankops-bot: FYI: Correspondent banks in our routing (our intermediary BNK-INTL) enforce beneficiary address for USD >10k for certain countries. Consider adding beneficiary address field to our wire instructions UI to reduce future returns. File: UX/BL-5012 submitted.

csm_john: Customer replied: "We will resend wire today and confirm when it's sent. Thanks for the extension." Will update once they confirm.

diane_billing: Great. Closing until we see remittance. Keeping ticket open.
